newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 1.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech Republic can not set any conditions for its entry into NATO, President Vaclav Havel said after meeting with the chairman of the North Atlantic Assembly, Karsten Voigt.

- The Czech National Bank's proposal for the privatisation of the four biggest Czech banks evoked varying reactions among politicians. The opposition has refused to endorse the plan to privatise the banks.
- SPT Telecom posted a net profit of almost 3.8 billion crowns in the first three quarters of 1996 on revenues of approximately 23.3 billion crowns.

- Miroslav Spacek, a representative of Ceska Posta, has confirmed increased tarifs for postal service. While the increase is not yet finalised, it is expected to range from 10 hellers to one crown per stamp.

- Up to 500 of Poldi Ocel's 5,600 employees may use their legal right to leave the company. Poldi Employees have only received a deposit on their wages and can currently leave the company and expect two months of severance pay.

- Ceska Sporitelna is offering its clients the first actual credit cards on the Czech market. Other banks will continue to offer debit cards. No other banks have announced plans to offer credit cards of their own.

- Trinecky Zelezarny is expecting considerably worse economic results than originally planned. While the company originally expected a gross profit of 420 million crowns has decreased to a loss of 754 million crowns after auditors found miscalculations in its books from previous years.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The price of shares on the capital market are continuing to decrease and experts do not see any positive signals that this trend will reverse itself in the near future.
- Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna may obtain aid from the state in its current crisis. The Health Ministry will consider three variants once Minister Strasky returns from his holiday.

- There are more private companies in the Czech Republic than in any other post-communist country. There are 68.4 private companies per thousand inhabitants which is even higher than the average of 43 private companies per thousand inhabitants in the EU.
PRAVO - The number of foreigners working in the Czech Republic has increased threefold since 1993.
- The state is likely to eliminate Chemicke Zavody Sokolov along the same lines as Aero Vodochody and CKD Praha Holding according to the Minister of Trade and Industry, Vladimir Dlouhy.
